interest: The 1940 'Hot Mikado' cartoon dispute and 1944 internal dissent urging abolition of the Japanese monarchy.
overview: Decimal file 894.001 H61 covers U.S. State Department records relating to Emperor Hirohito of Japan between January 1940 and May 1944. The prewar portion of the file (1940–1941) centers on diplomatic protocol, ceremonial greetings, and press friction concerning the sovereign, including presidential messages from Franklin D. Roosevelt on Hirohito's birthday and the 2600th anniversary of the founding of the Japanese Empire, internal discussions over the proper diplomatic style for addressing the Emperor, reports from Chile on local imperial birthday celebrations, and a diplomatic protest lodged by the Japanese Embassy over an American political cartoon caricaturing the Emperor as the 'Hot Mikado.' The wartime portion (1944) shifts sharply to critical policy debates concerning the postwar treatment of Japan, featuring cross-references on public and media inquiries about the imperial institution and biting internal memoranda submitted to Assistant Secretary Adolf A. Berle, Jr. that fiercely challenge the State Department's prevailing plans to preserve the Emperor and conduct an extensive military occupation.

subfiles.about: State Department record tracking the charge-out and transfer of various documents from decimal file 894.001 H61 between 1935 and 1942.
subfiles.from: Division of Communications and Records clerks
subfiles.summary: Charge slip for file 894.001 H61, 1935–1942.
subfiles.title: Department of State Charge Slip for File 894.001 H61
subfiles.to: Far Eastern Affairs and Political Relations divisions

subfiles.about: Internal memorandum recommending that President Roosevelt send a congratulatory message on the 2600th anniversary of the founding of the Japanese Empire.
subfiles.from: Cabot Coville (Division of Far Eastern Affairs)
subfiles.summary: FE favors a presidential message on February 11, 1940, for the 2600th anniversary, but advises not mentioning '2600th' or Emperor Jimmu.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from FE (Coville) to Summerlin regarding Congratulatory Message for Japanese 2600th Anniversary

subfiles.about: Ambassador Grew reports the Japanese Foreign Office designated February 11, 1940, as the appropriate date for foreign congratulations on the imperial anniversary.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew (U.S. Ambassador to Japan, Tokyo)
subfiles.summary: Grew reports the Foreign Office set February 11, 1940, as the date for congratulations on the 2600th anniversary of Emperor Jimmu's accession.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 44 from Ambassador Grew on Date for 2600th Anniversary Congratulations

subfiles.about: President Roosevelt conveys good wishes to Emperor Hirohito on the occasion of the Japanese imperial anniversary.
subfiles.from: Franklin D. Roosevelt (President of the United States)
subfiles.summary: Roosevelt's February 11, 1940 felicitations to Emperor Hirohito, avoiding mention of Jimmu or the 2600th anniversary.
subfiles.title: Telegram from President Roosevelt to Emperor Hirohito on the 2600th Anniversary

subfiles.about: The Department of State notifies the Tokyo Embassy that a presidential message will be transmitted to the Emperor on February 11.
subfiles.from: Cordell Hull (Secretary of State)
subfiles.summary: In telegram No. 53, the Department of State informs the American Embassy in Tokyo that a message from President Roosevelt will be sent to the Emperor on February 11. This cables serves as confirmation following Ambassador Grew's earlier inquiry in telegram No. 44.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 53 from State Department to American Embassy Tokyo

subfiles.about: The Department of State transmits the verbatim text of the President's February 11 telegram to the Tokyo Embassy for its records.
subfiles.from: Cordell Hull (Secretary of State)
subfiles.summary: Telegram No. 437 gives the Tokyo embassy the text of Roosevelt's February 11 message to Emperor Hirohito.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 437 from State Department to American Embassy Tokyo Transmitting Presidential Message Text

subfiles.about: Account of a diplomatic call by Japanese First Secretary Kase protesting an American newspaper cartoon depicting the Emperor.
subfiles.from: Joseph W. Ballantine (Division of Far Eastern Affairs)
subfiles.summary: Toshikazu Kase shows Ballantine the 'Hot Mikado' cartoon; Ballantine expresses regret, noting Kase was not agitated.
subfiles.title: Memorandum of Conversation between Joseph W. Ballantine and Toshikazu Kase on 'Hot Mikado' Cartoon

subfiles.about: Editorial cartoon depicting Emperor Hirohito as the 'Hot Mikado' struggling with diplomatic and economic difficulties.
subfiles.from: The Chicago Daily News
subfiles.summary: 'Hot Mikado' cartoon from the Chicago Daily News, January 29, 1940, showing Hirohito amid foreign and economic crises.
subfiles.title: Editorial Cartoon 'Hot Mikado' from the Chicago Daily News

subfiles.about: Reprint of the Chicago Daily News 'Hot Mikado' cartoon in the Sunday editorial pages of The Washington Post.
subfiles.from: The Washington Post
subfiles.summary: Washington Post reprint, February 4, 1940, of the 'Hot Mikado' cartoon, which prompted Japanese protests.
subfiles.title: Reprint of 'The Hot Mikado' Cartoon in The Washington Post

subfiles.about: Japanese Consul General Acino protests the publication of a caricature of Emperor Hirohito in the Chicago Daily News.
subfiles.from: Hirosi Acino (Consul General of Japan at Chicago)
subfiles.summary: Consul General Hirosi Acino protests to Paul Scott Mowrer that the 'Hot Mikado' cartoon disrespected Japan's sovereign.
subfiles.title: Letter from Japanese Consul General Hirosi Acino to Paul Scott Mowrer Protesting 'Hot Mikado' Cartoon
subfiles.to: Paul Scott Mowrer (Editor, The Chicago Daily News)

subfiles.about: Editor Paul Scott Mowrer defends freedom of the press and the democratic tradition of political satire while offering a courteous accommodation.
subfiles.from: Paul Scott Mowrer (Editor, The Chicago Daily News)
subfiles.summary: Paul Scott Mowrer replies that no offense was meant and declines special treatment, but will ask cartoonists to avoid depicting the Emperor.
subfiles.title: Letter from Editor Paul Scott Mowrer to Japanese Consul General Hirosi Acino Defending Press Freedom
subfiles.to: Hirosi Acino (Consul General of Japan at Chicago)

subfiles.about: Emperor Hirohito expresses appreciation to President Roosevelt for his message on the 2600th imperial anniversary.
subfiles.from: Hirohito (Emperor of Japan)
subfiles.summary: A telegram sent via RCA from Tokyo in which Emperor Hirohito acknowledges President Roosevelt's congratulatory message of February 11. The Emperor expresses his heartfelt thanks and great appreciation for the President's kind greetings. The document is filed under serial 894.001 H 61/126.
subfiles.title: Telegram from Emperor Hirohito to President Roosevelt Acknowledging Anniversary Message
subfiles.to: Franklin D. Roosevelt (President of the United States)

subfiles.about: Memorandum surveying diplomatic precedents regarding the official style and title used in addressing the Emperor of Japan.
subfiles.from: Schuler (Division of Far Eastern Affairs)
subfiles.summary: FE reviews past forms of addressing the Japanese Emperor and suggests asking the Tokyo embassy for the proper style.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from FE (Schuler) on Departmental Practice in Addressing the Japanese Sovereign

subfiles.about: President Roosevelt transmits official congratulations to Emperor Hirohito on the occasion of his birthday.
subfiles.from: Franklin D. Roosevelt (President of the United States)
subfiles.summary: President Roosevelt sends annual birthday felicitations to Emperor Hirohito in Tokyo via RCA. The text extends sincere felicitations upon the anniversary of the Emperor's birth and conveys best personal wishes. The message represents the routine execution of reciprocal head-of-state courtesies.
subfiles.title: Telegram from President Roosevelt to Emperor Hirohito on His Birthday

subfiles.about: White House transmittal slip routing Emperor Hirohito's birthday acknowledgment telegram to the State Department.
subfiles.from: Edwin M. Watson (Secretary to the President)
subfiles.summary: White House referral slip from Edwin M. Watson sending the Emperor's birthday reply to Summerlin.
subfiles.title: White House Referral Slip Transmitting Emperor Hirohito's Birthday Acknowledgment
subfiles.to: Department of State (Attention: George T. Summerlin)

subfiles.about: Emperor Hirohito thanks President Roosevelt for his congratulatory birthday greetings.
subfiles.from: Hirohito (Emperor of Japan)
subfiles.summary: A telegram transmitted from Tokyo via RCA in which Emperor Hirohito acknowledges President Roosevelt's birthday telegram. The Emperor expresses cordial thanks for the congratulations and good wishes received on his birthday. The telegram was stamped and filed under serial 894.001 H 61/127.
subfiles.title: Telegram from Emperor Hirohito to President Roosevelt Acknowledging Birthday Greetings
subfiles.to: Franklin D. Roosevelt (President of the United States)

subfiles.about: Ambassador Bowers reports on the observance of Emperor Hirohito's birthday in Chile and Japanese propaganda features in Santiago newspapers.
subfiles.from: Claude G. Bowers (U.S. Ambassador to Chile)
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Claude G. Bowers reports curtailed Emperor's birthday celebrations in Santiago and Japanese-subsidized newspaper features.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 488 from Ambassador Bowers on Japanese Anniversary Celebrations in Chile

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet citing intelligence on the Tripartite Pact and rumors of an extremist plot against Emperor Hirohito.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew (U.S. Ambassador to Japan, Tokyo)
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Tokyo telegram No. 954 (October 7, 1940) on the Tripartite Pact and rumored threats to the Emperor.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet on Tripartite Alliance and Military Rumors Concerning Emperor

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet citing guidance on Ambassador Grew's address for the 2600th imperial anniversary celebration.
subfiles.from: Cordell Hull (Secretary of State)
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to telegram No. 432 (October 31, 1940) suggesting revisions to Grew's 2600th anniversary address.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet on Suggested Revision of Ambassador Grew's Anniversary Address

subfiles.about: President Roosevelt extends birthday congratulations and best wishes to Emperor Hirohito in April 1941.
subfiles.from: Franklin D. Roosevelt (President of the United States)
subfiles.summary: Official outbound telegram from the White House conveying President Roosevelt's congratulations and best wishes to Emperor Hirohito on his birthday, April 29, 1941. The message represents the continuation of formal diplomatic protocol despite deteriorating relations between the two countries.
subfiles.title: Telegram from President Roosevelt to Emperor Hirohito on His 1941 Birthday

subfiles.about: White House routing slip transmitting Emperor Hirohito's 1941 birthday acknowledgment to the State Department.
subfiles.from: Edwin M. Watson (Secretary to the President)
subfiles.summary: White House referral slip routing Hirohito's 1941 birthday reply to George T. Summerlin; filed 894.001 H 61/131.
subfiles.title: White House Referral Slip for Emperor Hirohito's 1941 Birthday Reply
subfiles.to: Department of State (Attention: George T. Summerlin)

subfiles.about: Department record copy of President Roosevelt's April 29, 1941 birthday telegram to Emperor Hirohito.
subfiles.from: Franklin D. Roosevelt (President of the United States)
subfiles.summary: An official State Department duplicate/preparing office copy of President Roosevelt's 1941 birthday telegram to Emperor Hirohito, assigned serial number 894.001H61/130A. It records internal clearances through the Division of Far Eastern Affairs and the Division of Political Relations.
subfiles.title: Department Record Copy of President Roosevelt's 1941 Birthday Telegram to Emperor Hirohito

subfiles.about: Duplicate White House transmittal slip routing Emperor Hirohito's birthday acknowledgment to the State Department.
subfiles.from: Edwin M. Watson (Secretary to the President)
subfiles.summary: Duplicate White House referral slip sending the Emperor's birthday telegram to Summerlin, stamped May 1, 1941.
subfiles.title: Duplicate White House Referral Slip for Emperor Hirohito's Birthday Message
subfiles.to: Department of State (Attention: George T. Summerlin)

subfiles.about: Emperor Hirohito thanks President Roosevelt for birthday congratulations sent in April 1941.
subfiles.from: Hirohito (Emperor of Japan)
subfiles.summary: Incoming RCA telegram from Tokyo in which Emperor Hirohito expresses cordial thanks to President Roosevelt for his kind birthday message. This marked the final peaceful exchange of head-of-state birthday greetings between the United States and Japan prior to the outbreak of war in December 1941.
subfiles.title: Telegram from Emperor Hirohito to President Roosevelt Acknowledging 1941 Birthday Congratulations
subfiles.to: Franklin D. Roosevelt (President of the United States)

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet noting a Reuters press inquiry received by Mayor La Guardia regarding the postwar future of the Japanese Imperial House.
subfiles.from: Department of State
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to a January 20, 1944 letter to Mayor La Guardia on a Reuters query about keeping the Imperial House.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet on Postwar Maintenance of the Japanese Imperial House
subfiles.to: Fiorello H. La Guardia (Mayor of New York City)

subfiles.about: Surviving pages of a policy memorandum strongly arguing against an extended Allied occupation and rejecting retention of the Japanese Emperor.
subfiles.from: Robert G. Hooker, Jr. (R. G. H., Jr.)
subfiles.summary: Robert G. Hooker, Jr. urges destroying Japan's military capacity and withdrawing rather than a long occupation, rejecting retention of the Emperor.
subfiles.title: Memorandum by R. G. H., Jr. Critiquing Postwar Occupation and Retention of the Japanese Emperor
subfiles.to: Adolf A. Berle, Jr. (Assistant Secretary of State)

subfiles.about: Memorandum transmitting published articles on postwar policy toward Japan that diverge from State Department committee proposals.
subfiles.from: Robert G. Hooker, Jr. (R. G. H., Jr.)
subfiles.summary: R. G. H., Jr. sends Berle a summary of articles by Bisson, Peffer and Chamberlin that differ from Department postwar plans.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from R. G. H., Jr. to Assistant Secretary Berle on Postwar Policy Articles
subfiles.to: Adolf A. Berle, Jr. (Assistant Secretary of State)

subfiles.about: Memorandum commending Nathaniel Peffer's article arguing against prolonged military occupation of Japan and warning against preserving the Emperor.
subfiles.from: Robert G. Hooker, Jr. (R. G. H., Jr.)
subfiles.summary: R. G. H., Jr. commends Nathaniel Peffer's 'Occupy Japan?' to Berle, arguing that using the imperial institution is futile and dangerous.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from R. G. H., Jr. to Assistant Secretary Berle Commending Peffer's 'Occupy Japan?'
subfiles.to: Adolf A. Berle, Jr. (Assistant Secretary of State)

subfiles.about: Memorandum urging Assistant Secretary Berle to lead State Department opposition to retaining the Japanese imperial institution.
subfiles.from: Robert G. Hooker, Jr. (R. G. H., Jr.)
subfiles.summary: R. G. H., Jr. sends Berle a New Leader article urging abolition of the imperial institution, warning the issue is neglected.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from R. G. H., Jr. to Assistant Secretary Berle on Overthrowing the Japanese Imperial Institution
subfiles.to: Adolf A. Berle, Jr. (Assistant Secretary of State)
